#### 16.1.2 Alert Rules (config/prometheus/rules/buildtovalue.yml)

```yaml
# config/prometheus/rules/buildtovalue.yml

groups:
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Latency Alerts (SLO: p99 < 50ms)
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  - name: latency_alerts
    interval: 30s
    rules:
      - alert: HighP99Latency
        expr: |
          histogram_quantile(0.99, 
            rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])
          ) > 0.050
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: warning
          component: performance
        annotations:
          summary: "P99 latency above 50ms"
          description: |
            P99 latency is {{ $value | humanizeDuration }} (threshold: 50ms)
            Pod: {{ $labels.kubernetes_pod_name }}
            Namespace: {{ $labels.kubernetes_namespace }}
          runbook: https://docs.buildtovalue.com/runbooks/high-latency
      
      - alert: CriticalP99Latency
        expr: |
          histogram_quantile(0.99, 
            rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])
          ) > 0.100
        for: 2m
        labels:
          severity: critical
          component: performance
        annotations:
          summary: "P99 latency critically high (>100ms)"
          description: |
            P99 latency is {{ $value | humanizeDuration }} (critical threshold: 100ms)
            Pod: {{ $labels.kubernetes_pod_name }}
            IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED
          runbook: https://docs.buildtovalue.com/runbooks/critical-latency
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Error Rate Alerts (SLO: < 1% error rate)
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  - name: error_rate_alerts
    interval: 30s
    rules:
      - alert: HighErrorRate
        expr: |
          (
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (kubernetes_namespace)
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m])) by (kubernetes_namespace)
          ) > 0.01
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: warning
          component: reliability
        annotations:
          summary: "Error rate above 1%"
          description: |
            Error rate is {{ $value | humanizePercentage }}
            Namespace: {{ $labels.kubernetes_namespace }}
            5xx errors detected in last 5 minutes
          runbook: https://docs.buildtovalue.com/runbooks/high-error-rate
      
      - alert: CriticalErrorRate
        expr: |
          (
            sum(rate(http_requests_total{status=~"5.."}[5m])) by (kubernetes_namespace)
            /
            sum(rate(http_requests_total[5m])) by (kubernetes_namespace)
          ) > 0.05
        for: 2m
        labels:
          severity: critical
          component: reliability
        annotations:
          summary: "Error rate critically high (>5%)"
          description: |
            Error rate is {{ $value | humanizePercentage }}
            IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED - Service degradation
          runbook: https://docs.buildtovalue.com/runbooks/critical-error-rate
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Availability Alerts (SLO: 99.9% uptime)
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  - name: availability_alerts
    interval: 30s
    rules:
      - alert: ServiceDown
        expr: up{job="buildtovalue"} == 0
        for: 1m
        labels:
          severity: critical
          component: availability
        annotations:
          summary: "BuildToValue service is DOWN"
          description: |
            Pod {{ $labels.kubernetes_pod_name }} is unreachable
            Namespace: {{ $labels.kubernetes_namespace }}
            IMMEDIATE INVESTIGATION REQUIRED
          runbook: https://docs.buildtovalue.com/runbooks/service-down
      
      - alert: LowPodCount
        expr: |
          count(up{job="buildtovalue"} == 1) by (kubernetes_namespace) < 2
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: warning
          component: availability
        annotations:
          summary: "Less than 2 healthy pods running"
          description: |
            Only {{ $value }} pod(s) healthy in {{ $labels.kubernetes_namespace }}
            Minimum required: 2 (for high availability)
          runbook: https://docs.buildtovalue.com/runbooks/low-pod-count
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Resource Alerts (CPU/Memory)
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  - name: resource_alerts
    interval: 30s
    rules:
      - alert: HighCPUUsage
        expr: |
          (
            rate(process_cpu_seconds_total{job="buildtovalue"}[5m]) * 100
          ) > 80
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: warning
          component: resources
        annotations:
          summary: "High CPU usage (>80%)"
          description: |
            CPU usage is {{ $value | humanize }}%
            Pod: {{ $labels.kubernetes_pod_name }}
            Consider scaling horizontally
      
      - alert: HighMemoryUsage
        expr: |
          (
            process_resident_memory_bytes{job="buildtovalue"} 
            / 
            kube_pod_container_resource_limits{resource="memory"}
          ) > 0.85
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: warning
          component: resources
        annotations:
          summary: "High memory usage (>85%)"
          description: |
            Memory usage is {{ $value | humanizePercentage }}
            Pod: {{ $labels.kubernetes_pod_name }}
            Risk of OOMKill
      
      - alert: MemoryLeak
        expr: |
          rate(process_resident_memory_bytes{job="buildtovalue"}[30m]) > 1048576
        for: 1h
        labels:
          severity: warning
          component: resources
        annotations:
          summary: "Potential memory leak detected"
          description: |
            Memory growing at {{ $value | humanize }} bytes/sec
            Pod: {{ $labels.kubernetes_pod_name }}
            Investigation recommended
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Ethical Governance Alerts
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  - name: ethical_alerts
    interval: 1m
    rules:
      - alert: HighBlockRate
        expr: |
          (
            sum(rate(buildtovalue_decisions_total{action="BLOCK"}[15m]))
            /
            sum(rate(buildtovalue_decisions_total[15m]))
          ) > 0.30
        for: 15m
        labels:
          severity: warning
          component: ethical_governance
        annotations:
          summary: "High block rate (>30%)"
          description: |
            {{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of decisions are BLOCK
            Possible false positives or attack
            Review needed
      
      - alert: BiasDeclarationExpired
        expr: |
          (time() - buildtovalue_bias_calibration_timestamp) > (90 * 24 * 3600)
        for: 1h
        labels:
          severity: warning
          component: ethical_governance
        annotations:
          summary: "BiasDeclaration expired (>90 days)"
          description: |
            Last calibration: {{ $value | humanizeDuration }} ago
            Recalibration required for accuracy
          runbook: https://docs.buildtovalue.com/runbooks/bias-recalibration
      
      - alert: LowMercyScore
        expr: |
          avg(buildtovalue_mercy_score) < 0.2
        for: 1h
        labels:
          severity: info
          component: ethical_governance
        annotations:
          summary: "Consistently low mercy scores"
          description: |
            Average mercy score is {{ $value | humanize }}
            System may be too strict - ethical review recommended
      
      - alert: HighAppealRate
        expr: |
          (
            sum(rate(buildtovalue_appeals_total{result="success"}[24h]))
            /
            sum(rate(buildtovalue_decisions_total{action="BLOCK"}[24h]))
          ) > 0.10
        for: 1h
        labels:
          severity: warning
          component: ethical_governance
        annotations:
          summary: "High appeal success rate (>10%)"
          description: |
            {{ $value | humanizePercentage }} of appeals successful
            Policy adjustments may be needed
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Security Alerts
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  - name: security_alerts
    interval: 1m
    rules:
      - alert: RateLimitExceeded
        expr: |
          rate(buildtovalue_rate_limit_exceeded_total[5m]) > 10
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: warning
          component: security
        annotations:
          summary: "Rate limit frequently exceeded"
          description: |
            {{ $value }} rate limit violations per second
            Source IP: {{ $labels.source_ip }}
            Possible DDoS attempt
      
      - alert: AnomalousTrafficPattern
        expr: |
          (
            rate(http_requests_total[5m])
            /
            rate(http_requests_total[1h] offset 1h)
          ) > 5
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: warning
          component: security
        annotations:
          summary: "Traffic spike detected (5x normal)"
          description: |
            Current traffic: {{ $value }}x baseline
            Investigate for potential attack
      
      - alert: LedgerValidationFailure
        expr: |
          rate(buildtovalue_ledger_validation_failures_total[5m]) > 0
        for: 1m
        labels:
          severity: critical
          component: security
        annotations:
          summary: "Ledger validation failures detected"
          description: |
            {{ $value }} ledger validation failures
            POTENTIAL TAMPERING - IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED
          runbook: https://docs.buildtovalue.com/runbooks/ledger-tampering
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Database Alerts
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  - name: database_alerts
    interval: 30s
    rules:
      - alert: HighDatabaseConnections
        expr: |
          pg_stat_database_numbackends{datname="buildtovalue"} > 80
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: warning
          component: database
        annotations:
          summary: "High number of database connections"
          description: |
            {{ $value }} active connections (limit: 100)
            Connection pool may need tuning
      
      - alert: SlowQueries
        expr: |
          rate(pg_stat_statements_mean_exec_time{datname="buildtovalue"}[5m]) > 100
        for: 10m
        labels:
          severity: warning
          component: database
        annotations:
          summary: "Slow database queries detected"
          description: |
            Average query time: {{ $value }}ms
            Query optimization recommended
      
      - alert: DatabaseDiskSpaceLow
        expr: |
          (
            node_filesystem_avail_bytes{mountpoint="/var/lib/postgresql"}
            /
            node_filesystem_size_bytes{mountpoint="/var/lib/postgresql"}
          ) < 0.20
        for: 5m
        labels:
          severity: critical
          component: database
        annotations:
          summary: "Database disk space critically low (<20%)"
          description: |
            Available: {{ $value | humanizePercentage }}
            IMMEDIATE ACTION REQUIRED - Expand disk or cleanup
```

### 16.3 CUSTOM METRICS (RUST)

#### 16.3.1 Metrics Registry (src/kernel/metrics.rs)

```rust
// src/kernel/metrics.rs

use prometheus::{
    Counter, CounterVec, Histogram, HistogramVec, Gauge, GaugeVec,
    Registry, Opts, HistogramOpts,
};
use lazy_static::lazy_static;

lazy_static! {
    /// Global metrics registry
    pub static ref REGISTRY: Registry = Registry::new();
    
    // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    // Request Metrics
    // ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
    
    /// Total HTTP requests
    pub static ref HTTP_REQUESTS_TOTAL: CounterVec = {
        let opts = Opts::new(
            "http_requests_total",
            "Total number of HTTP requests"
        );
        let counter = CounterVec::new(opts, &["method", "status"]).unwrap();
        REGISTRY.register(Box::new(counter.clone())).unwrap();
        counter
    };
    
    /// HTTP request duration (histogram)
    pub static ref HTTP_REQUEST_DURATION: HistogramVec = {
        let opts = HistogramOpts::new(
            "http_request_duration_seconds",
            "HTTP request latencies in seconds"
        )
        .buckets(vec![
            0.001,  // 1ms
            0.005,  // 5ms
            0.010,  // 10ms
            0.025,  // 25ms
            0.050,  // 50ms
            0.075,  // 75ms
            0.100,  // 100ms
            0.250,  // 250ms
            0.500,  // 500ms
            1.000,  // 1s
        ]);
        
        let histogram = HistogramVec::new(opts, &["method", "endpoint"]).unwrap();
        REGISTRY.register(Box::new(histogram.clone())).unwrap();
        histogram
    };

}

/// Expose metrics for Prometheus scraping
pub fn metrics_handler() -> String {
    use prometheus::Encoder;
    
    let encoder = prometheus::TextEncoder::new();
    let metric_families = REGISTRY.gather();
    
    let mut buffer = Vec::new();
    encoder.encode(&metric_families, &mut buffer).unwrap();
    
    String::from_utf8(buffer).unwrap()
}

## PARTE 17: ALERTING & INCIDENT RESPONSE

### 17.1 ALERTMANAGER CONFIGURATION

#### 17.1.1 Alertmanager Config (config/alertmanager.yml)

```yaml
# config/alertmanager.yml

global:
  resolve_timeout: 5m
  
  # Slack global config
  slack_api_url: 'https://hooks.slack.com/services/YOUR_WEBHOOK_URL'
  
  # PagerDuty global config
  pagerduty_url: 'https://events.pagerduty.com/v2/enqueue'

# Templates for notifications
templates:
  - '/etc/alertmanager/templates/*.tmpl'

# Routing tree
route:
  # Default receiver
  receiver: 'slack-general'
  
  # Group alerts by these labels
  group_by: ['alertname', 'cluster', 'service']
  
  # Wait before sending first notification (allows grouping)
  group_wait: 30s
  
  # Wait before sending notification about new alerts in same group
  group_interval: 5m
  
  # Wait before re-sending notification for resolved/firing alerts
  repeat_interval: 4h
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Child routes (specific routing rules)
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  routes:
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # CRITICAL Alerts → PagerDuty (immediate escalation)
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    - match:
        severity: critical
      receiver: 'pagerduty-critical'
      group_wait: 10s
      group_interval: 1m
      repeat_interval: 1h
      continue: true  # Also send to Slack
    
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Ethical Governance Alerts → Ethical Committee
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    - match:
        component: ethical_governance
      receiver: 'slack-ethical-committee'
      group_wait: 1m
      group_interval: 10m
      repeat_interval: 12h
    
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Security Alerts → Security Team (high priority)
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    - match:
        component: security
      receiver: 'slack-security-team'
      group_wait: 30s
      group_interval: 5m
      repeat_interval: 2h
      routes:
        # Ledger tampering → CRITICAL escalation
        - match:
            alertname: LedgerValidationFailure
          receiver: 'pagerduty-security-incident'
          group_wait: 0s
          repeat_interval: 15m
    
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Performance Alerts → SRE Team
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    - match:
        component: performance
      receiver: 'slack-sre-team'
      group_wait: 1m
      group_interval: 5m
      repeat_interval: 3h
    
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    # Database Alerts → Database Team
    # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    - match:
        component: database
      receiver: 'slack-database-team'
      group_wait: 2m
      group_interval: 10m
      repeat_interval: 6h

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Inhibition Rules (suppress alerts)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
inhibit_rules:
  # Suppress low severity if critical is firing
  - source_match:
      severity: 'critical'
    target_match:
      severity: 'warning'
    equal: ['alertname', 'cluster', 'service']
  
  # Suppress HighErrorRate if ServiceDown
  - source_match:
      alertname: 'ServiceDown'
    target_match:
      alertname: 'HighErrorRate'
    equal: ['kubernetes_namespace']
  
  # Suppress resource alerts if pod is down
  - source_match:
      alertname: 'ServiceDown'
    target_match_re:
      alertname: '(HighCPUUsage|HighMemoryUsage)'
    equal: ['kubernetes_pod_name']

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Receivers (notification destinations)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
receivers:
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Slack: General Channel
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: 'slack-general'
    slack_configs:
      - channel: '#buildtovalue-alerts'
        icon_emoji: ':warning:'
        title: '{{ .GroupLabels.alertname }}'
        text: |
          {{ range .Alerts }}
          *Summary:* {{ .Annotations.summary }}
          *Description:* {{ .Annotations.description }}
          *Severity:* {{ .Labels.severity }}
          *Runbook:* {{ .Annotations.runbook }}
          {{ end }}
        send_resolved: true
        color: '{{ if eq .Status "firing" }}danger{{ else }}good{{ end }}'
  
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Slack: SRE Team
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: 'slack-sre-team'
    slack_configs:
      - channel: '#buildtovalue-sre'
        icon_emoji: ':fire:'
        title: '🔥 Performance Alert: {{ .GroupLabels.alertname }}'
        text: |
          {{ range .Alerts }}
          *Alert:* {{ .Labels.alertname }}
          *Pod:* {{ .Labels.kubernetes_pod_name }}
          *Namespace:* {{ .Labels.kubernetes_namespace }}
          *Description:* {{ .Annotations.description }}
          *Runbook:* <{{ .Annotations.runbook }}|View Runbook>
          {{ end }}
        send_resolved: true
  
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Slack: Ethical Committee
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: 'slack-ethical-committee'
    slack_configs:
      - channel: '#buildtovalue-ethical-committee'
        icon_emoji: ':balance_scale:'
        title: '⚖️ Ethical Governance Alert'
        text: |
          {{ range .Alerts }}
          *Alert:* {{ .Labels.alertname }}
          *Summary:* {{ .Annotations.summary }}
          *Description:* {{ .Annotations.description }}
          
          *Ethical Review Required*
          Please investigate and take appropriate action.
          {{ end }}
        send_resolved: true
        color: 'warning'
  
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Slack: Security Team
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: 'slack-security-team'
    slack_configs:
      - channel: '#buildtovalue-security'
        icon_emoji: ':shield:'
        title: '🛡️ Security Alert: {{ .GroupLabels.alertname }}'
        text: |
          {{ range .Alerts }}
          *SECURITY ALERT*
          *Type:* {{ .Labels.alertname }}
          *Severity:* {{ .Labels.severity }}
          *Description:* {{ .Annotations.description }}
          *Source:* {{ .Labels.source_ip | default "N/A" }}
          *Runbook:* <{{ .Annotations.runbook }}|Incident Response>
          {{ end }}
        send_resolved: true
        color: 'danger'
  
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Slack: Database Team
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: 'slack-database-team'
    slack_configs:
      - channel: '#buildtovalue-database'
        icon_emoji: ':database:'
        title: '🗄️ Database Alert'
        text: |
          {{ range .Alerts }}
          *Alert:* {{ .Labels.alertname }}
          *Database:* {{ .Labels.datname | default "N/A" }}
          *Description:* {{ .Annotations.description }}
          {{ end }}
        send_resolved: true
  
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # PagerDuty: Critical Incidents
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: 'pagerduty-critical'
    pagerduty_configs:
      - routing_key: 'YOUR_PAGERDUTY_INTEGRATION_KEY'
        description: |
          {{ .GroupLabels.alertname }}: {{ .CommonAnnotations.summary }}
        severity: 'critical'
        details:
          firing: '{{ .Alerts.Firing | len }}'
          resolved: '{{ .Alerts.Resolved | len }}'
          description: '{{ .CommonAnnotations.description }}'
          runbook: '{{ .CommonAnnotations.runbook }}'
  
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  # PagerDuty: Security Incidents
  # ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  - name: 'pagerduty-security-incident'
    pagerduty_configs:
      - routing_key: 'YOUR_PAGERDUTY_SECURITY_KEY'
        description: |
          SECURITY INCIDENT: {{ .GroupLabels.alertname }}
        severity: 'critical'
        details:
          alert_type: 'security'
          description: '{{ .CommonAnnotations.description }}'
          immediate_action: 'true'
```

### 17.2 INCIDENT RESPONSE RUNBOOKS

#### 17.2.1 High Latency Runbook (docs/runbooks/high-latency.md)

```markdown
# 🚨 RUNBOOK: High P99 Latency

**Alert Name:** `HighP99Latency` / `CriticalP99Latency`  
**Severity:** Warning (>50ms) / Critical (>100ms)  
**Component:** Performance  
**SLO Impact:** Yes (target: p99 < 50ms)

---

## 🎯 Symptom

P99 latency exceeds SLO threshold (50ms warning, 100ms critical).

---

## 📊 Diagnosis Steps

### 1. Check Grafana Dashboard

```
https://grafana.buildtovalue.com/d/main-dashboard
```

**Look for:**
- Latency spike timestamp
- Affected endpoints (check "Latency by Endpoint" panel)
- Correlation with traffic increase
- Error rate changes

### 2. Check Active Pods

```bash
kubectl get pods -n buildtovalue -o wide
```

**Verify:**
- All pods are `Running` (not `CrashLoopBackOff`)
- Pod age (recent restarts?)
- Node distribution (all on same node = problem)

### 3. Check Pod Metrics

```bash
# CPU usage
kubectl top pods -n buildtovalue

# Memory usage
kubectl describe pod <pod-name> -n buildtovalue | grep -A 5 "Limits"
```

**Red flags:**
- CPU > 80% of limit
- Memory > 85% of limit
- OOMKilled events in pod description

### 4. Check Application Logs

```bash
kubectl logs -n buildtovalue <pod-name> --tail=100 | grep -i "slow\|timeout\|error"
```

**Look for:**
- `SLOW_QUERY` warnings
- `FFI_TIMEOUT` errors
- `RUST_KERNEL_BLOCKED` messages

### 5. Query Prometheus

```promql
# P99 latency by endpoint
histogram_quantile(0.99, 
  sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, endpoint)
)

# Top slowest endpoints
topk(5, 
  histogram_quantile(0.99, 
    sum(rate(http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, endpoint)
  )
)

# Rust Kernel processing time
histogram_quantile(0.99, 
  rate(buildtovalue_kernel_processing_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])
)

# Python Governance processing time
histogram_quantile(0.99, 
  rate(buildtovalue_governance_processing_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])
)
```

---

## 🔧 Immediate Actions

### Scenario A: CPU Saturation

**Symptoms:**
- CPU usage > 80%
- High request rate
- Latency correlates with CPU

**Actions:**

```bash
# 1. Scale horizontally (add pods)
kubectl scale deployment buildtovalue -n buildtovalue --replicas=6

# 2. Monitor scaling
kubectl rollout status deployment/buildtovalue -n buildtovalue

# 3. Verify latency improvement
# (check Grafana after 2-3 minutes)
```

**Root Cause Investigation:**
- Check if traffic spike is legitimate (check Prometheus)
- Review recent code changes (CPU-intensive code added?)
- Profile CPU usage (use `pprof` if available)

---

### Scenario B: Memory Pressure

**Symptoms:**
- Memory usage > 85%
- OOMKilled events
- Pods restarting frequently

**Actions:**

```bash
# 1. Check memory leak (look for growing trend)
kubectl top pods -n buildtovalue --sort-by=memory

# 2. If leak confirmed, restart pods (rolling restart)
kubectl rollout restart deployment/buildtovalue -n buildtovalue

# 3. Increase memory limits (temporary fix)
kubectl set resources deployment/buildtovalue \
  -n buildtovalue \
  --limits=memory=3Gi \
  --requests=memory=1Gi
```

**Root Cause Investigation:**
- Check for memory leaks in Python (unreleased references?)
- Review Evidence Protocol (ring buffer overflow?)
- Check Ledger WAL size (growing unbounded?)

---

### Scenario C: Database Bottleneck

**Symptoms:**
- Slow queries in logs
- Database connection pool exhausted
- Latency spike correlates with DB operations

**Actions:**

```bash
# 1. Check database metrics
kubectl exec -it postgres-0 -n buildtovalue -- psql -U btv -d buildtovalue

# 2. Find slow queries
SELECT pid, now() - pg_stat_activity.query_start AS duration, query
FROM pg_stat_activity
WHERE state = 'active' AND now() - pg_stat_activity.query_start > interval '1 second'
ORDER BY duration DESC;

# 3. Kill slow queries (if needed)
SELECT pg_terminate_backend(pid) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE pid = <PID>;

# 4. Increase connection pool
# Edit config and redeploy
```

**Root Cause Investigation:**
- Missing indexes? (check EXPLAIN plans)
- Long-running transactions?
- Connection leak?

---

### Scenario D: Rust Kernel Blocked

**Symptoms:**
- `RUST_KERNEL_BLOCKED` in logs
- FFI timeout errors
- Validators taking too long

**Actions:**

```bash
# 1. Check which validator is slow
kubectl logs -n buildtovalue <pod-name> | grep "VALIDATOR_SLOW"

# 2. Temporarily disable slow validator (if non-critical)
# Edit profile YAML, set validator to disabled

# 3. Check for deadlock in Rust
kubectl exec -it <pod-name> -n buildtovalue -- \
  /bin/sh -c "kill -SIGUSR1 $(pgrep buildtovalue_kernel)"
# (SIGUSR1 dumps backtrace to stderr)
```

**Root Cause Investigation:**
- Infinite loop in validator?
- Blocking I/O operation?
- Mutex contention?

---

## 🛡️ Prevention

### Short-term (0-7 days)

- [ ] Increase HPA max replicas to 15
- [ ] Add more aggressive HPA scaling (scale at 60% CPU)
- [ ] Enable request caching (Redis) for repeated inputs

### Medium-term (1-4 weeks)

- [ ] Optimize hot paths (profile with `cargo flamegraph`)
- [ ] Add circuit breaker for slow validators
- [ ] Implement request coalescing (batch identical requests)

### Long-term (1-3 months)

- [ ] Migrate to async Rust (Tokio) for I/O operations
- [ ] Implement multi-tier caching (L1=memory, L2=Redis)
- [ ] Database query optimization (add indexes, partition tables)

---

## 📝 Post-Incident

### RCA Template

```markdown
# Post-Mortem: High P99 Latency Incident

**Date:** YYYY-MM-DD
**Duration:** XX minutes
**Impact:** X% of requests affected, p99 latency: XXms

## Timeline
- HH:MM - Alert fired
- HH:MM - Investigation started
- HH:MM - Root cause identified (CPU saturation)
- HH:MM - Mitigation applied (scaled to 6 pods)
- HH:MM - Latency normalized

## Action Items
- [ ] Item 1 (Owner: @person, Due: YYYY-MM-DD)
- [ ] Item 2 (Owner: @person, Due: YYYY-MM-DD)

## Lessons Learned

- What could be improved?
```

---

## 📞 Escalation

- **L1 (5 min):** On-call SRE
- **L2 (15 min):** SRE Team Lead + Backend Engineer
- **L3 (30 min):** VP Engineering + CTO

**Contact:** See PagerDuty escalation policy
```

#### 17.2.2 Service Down Runbook (docs/runbooks/service-down.md)

```markdown
# 🚨 RUNBOOK: Service Down

**Alert Name:** `ServiceDown`  
**Severity:** Critical  
**Component:** Availability  
**SLO Impact:** Yes (target: 99.9% uptime)

---

## 🎯 Symptom

BuildToValue service is completely unreachable (health check fails for >1 minute).

---

## 🚑 IMMEDIATE ACTIONS (< 5 minutes)

### Step 1: Verify Service State

```bash
# Check pod status
kubectl get pods -n buildtovalue

# Expected: At least 2 pods in "Running" state
# If ALL pods are down → CRITICAL
```

**Possible States:**

| State | Action |
|-------|--------|
| `Running` but health check fails | Go to Step 2 |
| `CrashLoopBackOff` | Go to Step 3 |
| `Pending` | Go to Step 4 |
| `ImagePullBackOff` | Go to Step 5 |
| No pods exist | Go to Step 6 |

---

### Step 2: Pods Running but Unhealthy

```bash
# Check pod logs
kubectl logs -n buildtovalue <pod-name> --tail=50

# Check events
kubectl describe pod <pod-name> -n buildtovalue
```

**Common Issues:**

**A) Port not listening:**
```bash
# Port forward and test
kubectl port-forward -n buildtovalue <pod-name> 8000:8000

# In another terminal
curl http://localhost:8000/health
```

**Fix:** Likely application startup issue. Check logs for errors.

**B) Liveness probe too aggressive:**
```bash
# Temporarily increase probe timeout
kubectl patch deployment buildtovalue -n buildtovalue --type='json' \
  -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/livenessProbe/timeoutSeconds","value":30}]'
```

---

### Step 3: CrashLoopBackOff

```bash
# Get recent logs (including previous crashes)
kubectl logs -n buildtovalue <pod-name> --previous

# Look for panic/error messages
```

**Common Causes:**

**A) Database unreachable:**
```bash
# Check Postgres
kubectl get pods -n buildtovalue | grep postgres

# Test connection
kubectl exec -it <buildtovalue-pod> -n buildtovalue -- \
  curl http://postgres-service:5432
```

**Fix:** Restart Postgres or fix network policy.

**B) Missing secrets:**
```bash
# Verify secrets exist
kubectl get secret buildtovalue-secrets -n buildtovalue

# Check if mounted correctly
kubectl describe pod <pod-name> -n buildtovalue | grep -A 5 "Mounts"
```

**Fix:** Re-create secret or fix deployment spec.

**C) Rust Kernel panic:**
```
# Look for "RUST PANIC" in logs
kubectl logs -n buildtovalue <pod-name> --previous | grep -i "panic"
```

**Fix:** Likely code bug. Rollback to previous version:
```bash
kubectl rollout undo deployment/buildtovalue -n buildtovalue
```

---

### Step 4: Pods Pending

```bash
# Check why pods can't be scheduled
kubectl describe pod <pod-name> -n buildtovalue | grep -A 10 "Events"
```

**Common Issues:**

**A) Insufficient resources:**
```
Events:
  ... FailedScheduling ... Insufficient cpu/memory
```

**Fix:** Scale down replicas or add nodes:
```bash
# Temporarily reduce replicas
kubectl scale deployment buildtovalue -n buildtovalue --replicas=2
```

**B) PersistentVolume not available:**
```
Events:
  ... FailedMount ... no persistent volumes available
```

**Fix:** Check PVC status:
```bash
kubectl get pvc -n buildtovalue
```

---

### Step 5: ImagePullBackOff

```bash
# Check image pull error
kubectl describe pod <pod-name> -n buildtovalue | grep -A 5 "Failed to pull image"
```

**Common Causes:**

**A) Image doesn't exist:**
- Tag is wrong
- Image was deleted
- Registry credentials expired

**Fix:**
```bash
# Check deployment image
kubectl get deployment buildtovalue -n buildtovalue -o yaml | grep "image:"

# Rollback to previous version
kubectl rollout undo deployment/buildtovalue -n buildtovalue
```

**B) Registry credentials missing:**
```bash
# Re-create image pull secret
kubectl create secret docker-registry regcred \
  --docker-server=ghcr.io \
  --docker-username=YOUR_USERNAME \
  --docker-password=YOUR_TOKEN \
  -n buildtovalue
```

---

### Step 6: No Pods Exist

```bash
# Check if deployment exists
kubectl get deployment -n buildtovalue

# If missing, re-apply
kubectl apply -f k8s/10-deployment.yaml
```

**Possible Causes:**
- Deployment was accidentally deleted
- Namespace was deleted
- Kubernetes cluster issue

---

## 🚨 IMMEDIATE ACTIONS (< 2 minutes)

### Step 1: STOP ALL WRITES

```bash
# 1. Set deployment to read-only mode
kubectl set env deployment/buildtovalue -n buildtovalue READONLY_MODE=true

# 2. Scale down to 1 replica (minimize damage)
kubectl scale deployment buildtovalue -n buildtovalue --replicas=1

# 3. Block external traffic (keep internal monitoring)
kubectl patch ingress buildtovalue-ingress -n buildtovalue --type=json \
  -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/metadata/annotations/nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io~1whitelist-source-range","value":"10.0.0.0/8"}]'
```

### Step 2: PRESERVE EVIDENCE

```bash
# 1. Copy ledger files
kubectl exec -n buildtovalue <pod-name> -- tar czf /tmp/ledger-backup.tar.gz /app/data/ledger
kubectl cp buildtovalue/<pod-name>:/tmp/ledger-backup.tar.gz ./ledger-evidence-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).tar.gz

# 2. Copy logs
kubectl logs -n buildtovalue --all-containers --timestamps > incident-logs-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).log

# 3. Export Prometheus metrics
curl http://prometheus:9090/api/v1/query_range?query=buildtovalue_ledger_validation_failures_total&start=$(date -u -d '1 hour ago' +%s)&end=$(date +%s)&step=15 > metrics-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).json

# 4. Upload to secure storage
aws s3 cp ledger-evidence-*.tar.gz s3://buildtovalue-security-incidents/ --sse
```

## 🛡️ CONTAINMENT (10-30 minutes)

### Determine Attack Vector

**Scenario A: External Attack**
- Source IP in logs is external
- Access via public API
- Authentication bypass suspected

**Actions:**
```bash
# Block attacker IP
kubectl patch ingress buildtovalue-ingress -n buildtovalue --type=json \
  -p='[{"op":"add","path":"/metadata/annotations/nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io~1deny-list","value":"<ATTACKER_IP>"}]'

# Rotate API keys
kubectl delete secret buildtovalue-secrets -n buildtovalue
kubectl create secret generic buildtovalue-secrets --from-file=./new-secrets/
kubectl rollout restart deployment/buildtovalue -n buildtovalue
```

---

**Scenario B: Internal Attack**
- Source is internal pod/service
- Possible compromised container
- Privilege escalation

**Actions:**
```bash
# Isolate compromised pod
kubectl delete pod <compromised-pod> -n buildtovalue

# Check for malicious containers
kubectl get pods -n buildtovalue -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.spec.containers[].image | contains("malicious"))'

# Review RBAC permissions
kubectl auth can-i --list --as=system:serviceaccount:buildtovalue:default
```

---

**Scenario C: Insider Threat**
- Access from legitimate user account
- Credentials may be compromised or misused

**Actions:**
```bash
# Revoke all access tokens
kubectl exec -it postgres-0 -n buildtovalue -- psql -U btv -d buildtovalue -c "UPDATE api_tokens SET revoked=true WHERE created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days';"

# Force password reset
# (send notification to all users)

# Enable MFA requirement
kubectl set env deployment/buildtovalue -n buildtovalue ENFORCE_MFA=true
```

### 18.1 INFRASTRUCTURE SECURITY

#### 18.1.1 Kubernetes Security Policies

```yaml
# k8s/security/pod-security-policy.yaml

apiVersion: policy/v1beta1
kind: PodSecurityPolicy
metadata:
  name: buildtovalue-restricted
  annotations:
    seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/allowedProfileNames: 'runtime/default'
    apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/allowedProfileNames: 'runtime/default'
    seccomp.security.alpha.kubernetes.io/defaultProfileName: 'runtime/default'
    apparmor.security.beta.kubernetes.io/defaultProfileName: 'runtime/default'
spec:
  # Privilege escalation
  privileged: false
  allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  
  # Required drop capabilities
  requiredDropCapabilities:
    - ALL
  
  # Allowed capabilities (minimal)
  allowedCapabilities: []
  
  # Volumes
  volumes:
    - 'configMap'
    - 'emptyDir'
    - 'projected'
    - 'secret'
    - 'downwardAPI'
    - 'persistentVolumeClaim'
  
  # Host namespaces
  hostNetwork: false
  hostIPC: false
  hostPID: false
  
  # Run as non-root
  runAsUser:
    rule: 'MustRunAsNonRoot'
  
  # SELinux
  seLinux:
    rule: 'RunAsAny'
  
  # Supplemental groups
  supplementalGroups:
    rule: 'RunAsAny'
  
  # FSGroup
  fsGroup:
    rule: 'RunAsAny'
  
  # Read-only root filesystem
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true

---
# k8s/security/network-policy.yaml

apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: buildtovalue-network-policy
  namespace: buildtovalue
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: buildtovalue
  
  policyTypes:
    - Ingress
    - Egress
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Ingress Rules (what can connect TO buildtovalue)
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  ingress:
    # Allow from Ingress Controller
    - from:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              name: ingress-nginx
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8000
    
    # Allow Prometheus scraping
    - from:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              name: monitoring
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 9090
    
    # Allow from same namespace (pod-to-pod)
    - from:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: buildtovalue
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 8000
  
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  # Egress Rules (what buildtovalue can connect TO)
  # ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
  egress:
    # Allow DNS resolution
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector:
            matchLabels:
              name: kube-system
      ports:
        - protocol: UDP
          port: 53
    
    # Allow PostgreSQL
    - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: postgres
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 5432
    
    # Allow Redis
    - to:
        - podSelector:
            matchLabels:
              app: redis
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 6379
    
    # Allow HTTPS external (for remote sync, etc)
    - to:
        - namespaceSelector: {}
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 443
    
    # Block everything else (default deny)

---
# k8s/security/rbac.yaml

apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: buildtovalue-sa
  namespace: buildtovalue

---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
kind: Role
metadata:
  name: buildtovalue-role
  namespace: buildtovalue
rules:
  # Read-only access to ConfigMaps
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["configmaps"]
    verbs: ["get", "list"]
  
  # Read-only access to Secrets (only specific ones)
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["secrets"]
    resourceNames: ["buildtovalue-secrets"]

  # Read-only access to own pods
  - apiGroups: [""]
    resources: ["pods"]

  # No write access, no exec, no delete

---
apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1

metadata:
  name: buildtovalue-rolebinding
  namespace: buildtovalue
roleRef:
  apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  kind: Role
  name: buildtovalue-role
subjects:
  - kind: ServiceAccount
    name: buildtovalue-sa
    namespace: buildtovalue

**How to use Sealed Secrets:**

```bash
# 1. Install sealed-secrets controller
kubectl apply -f https://github.com/bitnami-labs/sealed-secrets/releases/download/v0.24.0/controller.yaml

# 2. Install kubeseal CLI
wget https://github.com/bitnami-labs/sealed-secrets/releases/download/v0.24.0/kubeseal-linux-amd64 -O kubeseal
chmod +x kubeseal
sudo mv kubeseal /usr/local/bin/

# 3. Create sealed secret
echo -n "postgresql://user:password@host:5432/db" | \
  kubeseal --raw --from-file=/dev/stdin \
  --namespace=buildtovalue \
  --name=buildtovalue-secrets \
  --scope=strict

# 4. Apply sealed secret
kubectl apply -f k8s/security/sealed-secret.yaml
```

### 18.2 APPLICATION SECURITY

#### 18.2.1 Input Validation & Sanitization (src/kernel/validators/input_sanitizer.rs)

```rust
// src/kernel/validators/input_sanitizer.rs

use unicode_normalization::UnicodeNormalization;
use std::borrow::Cow;

/// Input sanitizer (defense in depth)
pub struct InputSanitizer {
    max_length: usize,
    allow_unicode: bool,
}

impl InputSanitizer {
    pub fn new(max_length: usize) -> Self {
        Self {
            max_length,
            allow_unicode: true,
        }
    }
    
    /// Sanitiza input completo (pipeline)
    pub fn sanitize(&self, input: &str) -> Result<String, SanitizationError> {
        let mut text = Cow::Borrowed(input);
        
        // 1. Length check (prevent DoS)
        if text.len() > self.max_length {
            return Err(SanitizationError::InputTooLarge {
                size: text.len(),
                max: self.max_length,
            });
        }
        
        // 2. Unicode normalization (NFC form)
        text = Cow::Owned(text.nfc().collect::<String>());
        
        // 3. Remove zero-width characters (evasion prevention)
        text = Cow::Owned(self.remove_zero_width(&text));
        
        // 4. Remove control characters (except whitespace)
        text = Cow::Owned(self.remove_control_chars(&text));
        
        // 5. Normalize whitespace
        text = Cow::Owned(self.normalize_whitespace(&text));
        
        // 6. Validate UTF-8 (防止 invalid sequences)
        if !text.is_char_boundary(text.len()) {
            return Err(SanitizationError::InvalidUtf8);
        }
        
        // 7. Check for null bytes (C-string injection prevention)
        if text.contains('\0') {
            return Err(SanitizationError::NullByteDetected);
        }
        
        Ok(text.into_owned())
    }
    
    /// Remove zero-width characters
    fn remove_zero_width(&self, text: &str) -> String {
        text.chars()
            .filter(|&c| {
                !matches!(c,
                    '\u{200B}' |  // Zero-width space
                    '\u{200C}' |  // Zero-width non-joiner
                    '\u{200D}' |  // Zero-width joiner
                    '\u{FEFF}'    // Zero-width no-break space
                )
            })
            .collect()
    }
    
    /// Remove control characters (except tab, newline, carriage return)
    fn remove_control_chars(&self, text: &str) -> String {
        text.chars()
            .filter(|&c| {
                !c.is_control() || matches!(c, '\t' | '\n' | '\r')
            })
            .collect()
    }
    
    /// Normalize whitespace (collapse multiple spaces)
    fn normalize_whitespace(&self, text: &str) -> String {
        text.split_whitespace().collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" ")
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum SanitizationError {
    #[error("Input too large: {size} bytes (max: {max})")]
    InputTooLarge { size: usize, max: usize },
    
    #[error("Invalid UTF-8 encoding")]
    InvalidUtf8,
    
    #[error("Null byte detected (possible injection)")]
    NullByteDetected,
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    
    #[test]
    fn test_zero_width_removal() {
        let sanitizer = InputSanitizer::new(1024);
        
        // CPF with zero-width spaces
        let input = "123\u{200B}.456\u{200B}.789\u{200B}-09";
        let output = sanitizer.sanitize(input).unwrap();
        
        assert_eq!(output, "123.456.789-09");
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn test_control_char_removal() {
        let sanitizer = InputSanitizer::new(1024);
        
        // Text with control characters
        let input = "Hello\x00World\x01Test";
        let result = sanitizer.sanitize(input);
        
        // Should fail due to null byte
        assert!(result.is_err());
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn test_length_limit() {
        let sanitizer = InputSanitizer::new(10);
        
        let input = "This is a very long text";
        let result = sanitizer.sanitize(input);
        
        assert!(matches!(result, Err(SanitizationError::InputTooLarge { .. })));
    }
}

#### 18.2.2 SQL Injection Prevention (src/governance/database.py)

```python
# src/governance/database.py

from sqlalchemy import create_engine, text
from sqlalchemy.orm import sessionmaker
from sqlalchemy.pool import NullPool
import logging

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)

class SecureDatabase:
    """
    Database wrapper com proteção contra SQL injection.
    
    Princípios:
    1. NUNCA concatenar strings em queries
    2. Sempre usar parametrized queries
    3. Validar inputs antes de usar
    4. Limitar privilégios do DB user
    """
    
    def __init__(self, connection_string: str):
        # Connection string validation
        if not connection_string.startswith(('postgresql://', 'postgres://')):
            raise ValueError("Invalid database connection string")
        
        # Create engine (no privilege escalation)
        self.engine = create_engine(
            connection_string,
            poolclass=NullPool,  # No connection pooling (security)
            echo=False,  # No SQL logging (prevent credential leaks)
            isolation_level="READ COMMITTED",
        )
        
        self.SessionLocal = sessionmaker(bind=self.engine)
    
    def execute_query(self, query: str, params: dict = None) -> list:
        """
        Executa query parametrizada (SQL injection safe).
        
        CORRETO:
        >>> db.execute_query("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = :id", {"id": user_id})
        
        INCORRETO (VULNERÁVEL):
        >>> db.execute_query(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {user_id}")
        """
        if params is None:
            params = {}
        
        # Valida que query não contém string interpolation
        if any(marker in query for marker in ['%s', '%d', '{', '}']):
            raise ValueError(
                "Query contains string interpolation markers. "
                "Use parameterized queries with :param syntax."
            )
        
        with self.SessionLocal() as session:
            try:
                result = session.execute(text(query), params)
                return result.fetchall()
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Query execution failed: {e}")
                session.rollback()
                raise
    
    def insert_appeal(self, session_id: str, verdict_id: str, reason: str) -> int:
        """
        Insere apelação (exemplo de query parametrizada).
        """
        query = """
            INSERT INTO appeals (session_id, verdict_id, reason, timestamp)
            VALUES (:session_id, :verdict_id, :reason, NOW())
            RETURNING id
        """
        
        params = {
            "session_id": session_id,
            "verdict_id": verdict_id,
            "reason": reason,  # Não sanitizado aqui (DB faz escape)
        }
        
        result = self.execute_query(query, params)
        return result[0][0]
    
    def get_trust_score(self, session_id: str) -> float:
        """
        Busca trust score (safe query).
        """
        query = """
            SELECT trust_score
            FROM user_sessions
            WHERE session_id = :session_id
        """
        
        result = self.execute_query(query, {"session_id": session_id})
        
        if result:
            return float(result[0][0])
        return 0.0

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# EXEMPLOS DE USO
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

# ✅ CORRETO (parametrizado)
def get_user_safe(db: SecureDatabase, user_id: int):
    query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = :id"
    return db.execute_query(query, {"id": user_id})

# ❌ INCORRETO (SQL injection vulnerável)
def get_user_unsafe(db: SecureDatabase, user_id: int):
    # NUNCA FAÇA ISSO!
    query = f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = {user_id}"
    return db.execute_query(query)
    # Se user_id = "1 OR 1=1", retorna TODOS os usuários!

# ✅ CORRETO (múltiplos parâmetros)
def search_users_safe(db: SecureDatabase, name: str, email: str):
    query = """
        SELECT * FROM users
        WHERE name LIKE :name AND email = :email
    """
    return db.execute_query(query, {
        "name": f"%{name}%",
        "email": email,
    })

# ❌ INCORRETO (SQL injection via LIKE)
def search_users_unsafe(db: SecureDatabase, name: str):
    # NUNCA FAÇA ISSO!
    query = f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE name LIKE '%{name}%'"
    return db.execute_query(query)
    # Se name = "'; DROP TABLE users; --", destrói tabela!

#### 18.2.3 XSS Prevention (src/api/response_sanitizer.py)

```python
# src/api/response_sanitizer.py

import html
import re
from typing import Any, Dict

class ResponseSanitizer:
    """
    Sanitiza responses para prevenir XSS (Cross-Site Scripting).
    
    Princípios:
    1. Escape HTML entities
    2. Remove scripts
    3. Sanitize URLs
    4. Content-Type headers corretos
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def sanitize_html(text: str) -> str:
        """
        Escape HTML entities (previne XSS).
        
        Exemplos:
        - "<script>alert('xss')</script>" → "&lt;script&gt;alert('xss')&lt;/script&gt;"
        - "Hello <b>World</b>" → "Hello &lt;b&gt;World&lt;/b&gt;"
        """
        return html.escape(text, quote=True)
    
    @staticmethod
    def remove_scripts(text: str) -> str:
        """
        Remove tags <script> (defense in depth).
        """
        # Remove script tags (case-insensitive)
        text = re.sub(r'<script[^>]*>.*?</script>', '', text, flags=re.IGNORECASE | re.DOTALL)
        
        # Remove event handlers (onclick, onerror, etc)
        text = re.sub(r'\s*on\w+\s*=\s*["\'].*?["\']', '', text, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
        
        # Remove javascript: URLs
        text = re.sub(r'javascript:', '', text, flags=re.IGNORECASE)
        
        return text
    
    @staticmethod
    def sanitize_json_response(data: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Sanitiza recursivamente um JSON response.
        """
        if isinstance(data, dict):
            return {
                key: ResponseSanitizer.sanitize_json_response(value)
                for key, value in data.items()
            }
        elif isinstance(data, list):
            return [ResponseSanitizer.sanitize_json_response(item) for item in data]
        elif isinstance(data, str):
            # Sanitiza strings (HTML escape)
            return ResponseSanitizer.sanitize_html(data)
        else:
            return data
    
    @staticmethod
    def get_safe_headers() -> Dict[str, str]:
        """
        Headers de segurança (XSS, clickjacking, etc).
        """
        return {
            # XSS Protection
            "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
            "X-Frame-Options": "DENY",
            "X-XSS-Protection": "1; mode=block",
            
            # Content Security Policy
            "Content-Security-Policy": (
                "default-src 'self'; "
                "script-src 'self'; "
                "style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; "
                "img-src 'self' data: https:; "
                "font-src 'self'; "
                "connect-src 'self'; "
                "frame-ancestors 'none';"
            ),
            
            # HTTPS enforcement
            "Strict-Transport-Security": "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains",
            
            # Referrer policy
            "Referrer-Policy": "strict-origin-when-cross-origin",
            
            # Permissions policy
            "Permissions-Policy": "geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=()",
        }

# FastAPI middleware para aplicar headers
from fastapi import Request, Response
from starlette.middleware.base import BaseHTTPMiddleware

class SecurityHeadersMiddleware(BaseHTTPMiddleware):
    async def dispatch(self, request: Request, call_next):
        response = await call_next(request)
        
        # Adiciona headers de segurança
        for key, value in ResponseSanitizer.get_safe_headers().items():
            response.headers[key] = value
        
        return response

# Uso no FastAPI
from fastapi import FastAPI

app = FastAPI()
app.add_middleware(SecurityHeadersMiddleware)

@app.post("/api/v2/validate")
async def validate_input(text: str):
    # Process input...
    result = {
        "action": "BLOCK",
        "rationale": "CPF detected in general context",
        "user_input": text,  # ← DANGER: XSS se não sanitizado!
    }
    
    # Sanitiza response
    safe_result = ResponseSanitizer.sanitize_json_response(result)
    
    return safe_result

### 18.3 CRYPTOGRAPHY

#### 18.3.1 Signing Key Management (src/kernel/crypto/signing.rs)

```rust
// src/kernel/crypto/signing.rs

use ring::hmac;
use std::fs;
use std::path::Path;

/// Signing key manager (HMAC-SHA256)
pub struct SigningKeyManager {
    key: hmac::Key,
}

impl SigningKeyManager {
    /// Load signing key from file (secure storage)
    pub fn from_file<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> Result<Self, CryptoError> {
        // Read key file
        let key_bytes = fs::read(path.as_ref())
            .map_err(|e| CryptoError::KeyLoadFailed(e.to_string()))?;
        
        // Validate key length (must be 32 bytes for HMAC-SHA256)
        if key_bytes.len() != 32 {
            return Err(CryptoError::InvalidKeyLength {
                expected: 32,
                actual: key_bytes.len(),
            });
        }
        
        // Validate key entropy (must not be all zeros, etc)
        if key_bytes.iter().all(|&b| b == 0) {
            return Err(CryptoError::WeakKey("Key is all zeros".to_string()));
        }
        
        let key = hmac::Key::new(hmac::HMAC_SHA256, &key_bytes);
        
        // Securely zero out key_bytes (prevent leaks)
        drop(key_bytes);
        
        Ok(Self { key })
    }
    
    /// Generate new signing key (for initial setup)
    pub fn generate() -> Result<Vec<u8>, CryptoError> {
        use ring::rand::{SystemRandom, SecureRandom};
        
        let rng = SystemRandom::new();
        let mut key_bytes = vec![0u8; 32];
        
        rng.fill(&mut key_bytes)
            .map_err(|_| CryptoError::KeyGenerationFailed)?;
        
        Ok(key_bytes)
    }
    
    /// Sign message (HMAC-SHA256)
    pub fn sign(&self, message: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        let signature = hmac::sign(&self.key, message);
        signature.as_ref().to_vec()
    }
    
    /// Verify signature (constant-time comparison)
    pub fn verify(&self, message: &[u8], signature: &[u8]) -> bool {
        hmac::verify(&self.key, message, signature).is_ok()
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, thiserror::Error)]
pub enum CryptoError {
    #[error("Failed to load key: {0}")]
    KeyLoadFailed(String),
    
    #[error("Invalid key length: expected {expected}, got {actual}")]
    InvalidKeyLength { expected: usize, actual: usize },
    
    #[error("Weak key detected: {0}")]
    WeakKey(String),
    
    #[error("Key generation failed")]
    KeyGenerationFailed,
}

// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
// Key Rotation Support
// ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

pub struct SigningKeyRotator {
    current_key: SigningKeyManager,
    previous_keys: Vec<SigningKeyManager>,
}

impl SigningKeyRotator {
    /// Load current key + previous keys (for rotation)
    pub fn new(
        current_key_path: &Path,
        previous_key_paths: Vec<&Path>,
    ) -> Result<Self, CryptoError> {
        let current_key = SigningKeyManager::from_file(current_key_path)?;
        
        let mut previous_keys = Vec::new();
        for path in previous_key_paths {
            previous_keys.push(SigningKeyManager::from_file(path)?);
        }
        
        Ok(Self {
            current_key,
            previous_keys,
        })
    }
    
    /// Sign with current key
    pub fn sign(&self, message: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        self.current_key.sign(message)
    }
    
    /// Verify with current key OR previous keys (during rotation)
    pub fn verify(&self, message: &[u8], signature: &[u8]) -> bool {
        // Try current key first
        if self.current_key.verify(message, signature) {
            return true;
        }
        
        // Try previous keys (rotation period)
        for key in &self.previous_keys {
            if key.verify(message, signature) {
                return true;
            }
        }
        
        false
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use std::io::Write;
    use tempfile::NamedTempFile;
    
    #[test]
    fn test_sign_and_verify() {
        // Generate key
        let key_bytes = SigningKeyManager::generate().unwrap();
        
        // Write to temp file
        let mut temp_file = NamedTempFile::new().unwrap();
        temp_file.write_all(&key_bytes).unwrap();
        
        // Load key
        let manager = SigningKeyManager::from_file(temp_file.path()).unwrap();
        
        // Sign message
        let message = b"Hello, World!";
        let signature = manager.sign(message);
        
        // Verify
        assert!(manager.verify(message, &signature));
        
        // Verify with wrong message
        assert!(!manager.verify(b"Wrong message", &signature));
    }
    
    #[test]
    fn test_key_rotation() {
        // Generate keys
        let key1 = SigningKeyManager::generate().unwrap();
        let key2 = SigningKeyManager::generate().unwrap();
        
        // Write to temp files
        let mut file1 = NamedTempFile::new().unwrap();
        let mut file2 = NamedTempFile::new().unwrap();
        file1.write_all(&key1).unwrap();
        file2.write_all(&key2).unwrap();
        
        // Create rotator (key2 = current, key1 = previous)
        let rotator = SigningKeyRotator::new(
            file2.path(),
            vec![file1.path()],
        ).unwrap();
        
        // Sign with current key
        let message = b"Test message";
        let signature_current = rotator.sign(message);
        
        // Should verify (current key)
        assert!(rotator.verify(message, &signature_current));
        
        // Sign with previous key manually
        let manager_previous = SigningKeyManager::from_file(file1.path()).unwrap();
        let signature_previous = manager_previous.sign(message);
        
        // Should also verify (previous key)
        assert!(rotator.verify(message, &signature_previous));
    }
}

#### 18.3.2 Key Generation Script (scripts/generate_signing_key.sh)

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# scripts/generate_signing_key.sh

set -euo pipefail

KEY_FILE="${1:-secrets/signing_key.bin}"
KEY_DIR=$(dirname "$KEY_FILE")

echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo "BuildToValue - Signing Key Generator"
echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo ""

# Check if key already exists
if [[ -f "$KEY_FILE" ]]; then
    echo "❌ ERROR: Key file already exists: $KEY_FILE"
    echo ""
    echo "To rotate key, use: ./scripts/rotate_signing_key.sh"
    exit 1
fi

# Create directory
mkdir -p "$KEY_DIR"

# Generate 32 random bytes (256 bits)
echo "🔐 Generating 32-byte signing key..."
openssl rand -out "$KEY_FILE" 32

# Set restrictive permissions
chmod 400 "$KEY_FILE"

# Calculate hash (for verification)
KEY_HASH=$(openssl dgst -sha256 "$KEY_FILE" | awk '{print $2}')

echo "✅ Signing key generated successfully!"
echo ""
echo "📁 Location: $KEY_FILE"
echo "🔒 Permissions: 400 (read-only, owner only)"
echo "🔑 SHA256: $KEY_HASH"
echo ""
echo "⚠️  IMPORTANT:"
echo "   - Store this key securely (vault, KMS, etc.)"
echo "   - Never commit to Git"
echo "   - Rotate every 90 days"
echo "   - Backup securely"
echo ""

# Add to .gitignore
if ! grep -q "$KEY_FILE" .gitignore 2>/dev/null; then
    echo "$KEY_FILE" >> .gitignore
    echo "✅ Added to .gitignore"
fi

# Create backup
BACKUP_FILE="$KEY_DIR/signing_key_backup_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).bin"
cp "$KEY_FILE" "$BACKUP_FILE"
chmod 400 "$BACKUP_FILE"

echo "💾 Backup created: $BACKUP_FILE"
echo ""
echo "Next steps:"
echo "  1. Store backup in secure location (off-site)"
echo "  2. Deploy key to production (Kubernetes secret)"
echo "  3. Update SIGNING_KEY_PATH in config"
echo "  4. Test signature verification"
echo ""

#### 18.3.3 Key Rotation Script (scripts/rotate_signing_key.sh)

```bash
#!/bin/bash
# scripts/rotate_signing_key.sh

set -euo pipefail

CURRENT_KEY="secrets/signing_key.bin"
PREVIOUS_KEY="secrets/signing_key_previous.bin"

echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo "BuildToValue - Signing Key Rotation"
echo "═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════"
echo ""

# Verify current key exists
if [[ ! -f "$CURRENT_KEY" ]]; then
    echo "❌ ERROR: Current key not found: $CURRENT_KEY"
    exit 1
fi

echo "🔄 Rotating signing key..."
echo ""

# Backup current key as previous
if [[ -f "$PREVIOUS_KEY" ]]; then
    echo "⚠️  Previous key already exists, archiving..."
    ARCHIVE_KEY="secrets/signing_key_archive_$(date +%Y%m%d_%H%M%S).bin"
    mv "$PREVIOUS_KEY" "$ARCHIVE_KEY"
    echo "   Archived: $ARCHIVE_KEY"
fi

mv "$CURRENT_KEY" "$PREVIOUS_KEY"
echo "✅ Current key → Previous key"

# Generate new key
openssl rand -out "$CURRENT_KEY" 32
chmod 400 "$CURRENT_KEY"

# Calculate hashes
CURRENT_HASH=$(openssl dgst -sha256 "$CURRENT_KEY" | awk '{print $2}')
PREVIOUS_HASH=$(openssl dgst -sha256 "$PREVIOUS_KEY" | awk '{print $2}')

echo "✅ New key generated"
echo ""
echo "📊 Key Status:"
echo "   Current:  $CURRENT_HASH"
echo "   Previous: $PREVIOUS_HASH"
echo ""

# Update Kubernetes secret
echo "🚀 Updating Kubernetes secret..."

kubectl create secret generic buildtovalue-secrets-new \
    --from-file=SIGNING_KEY="$CURRENT_KEY" \
    --from-file=SIGNING_KEY_PREVIOUS="$PREVIOUS_KEY" \
    --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -

echo "✅ Kubernetes secret updated"
echo ""

# Rolling restart
echo "🔄 Performing rolling restart..."
kubectl rollout restart deployment/buildtovalue -n buildtovalue
kubectl rollout status deployment/buildtovalue -n buildtovalue --timeout=5m

echo ""
echo "✅ Key rotation completed successfully!"
echo ""
echo "📝 Post-rotation checklist:"
echo "   - [ ] Verify service is healthy"
echo "   - [ ] Test signature verification (old + new keys)"
echo "   - [ ] Monitor error logs (24 hours)"
echo "   - [ ] Remove previous key after grace period (30 days)"
echo "   - [ ] Update key rotation log"
echo ""
```

## PARTE 19: TROUBLESHOOTING GUIDE & FAQ

### 19.1 COMMON ISSUES & SOLUTIONS

#### 19.1.1 High Latency Issues

```markdown
# Issue: P99 Latency > 50ms

## Symptoms
- Prometheus alert: HighP99Latency
- Slow API responses
- User complaints about performance

## Diagnosis

### Step 1: Identify Bottleneck Layer

**Check Grafana Dashboard:**
```
Main Dashboard → Latency Breakdown Panel
```

Look for which component is slow:
- Rust Kernel processing: > 30ms
- Python Governance: > 10ms
- Database queries: > 5ms
- FFI overhead: > 2ms

### Step 2: Rust Kernel Slow

**Symptoms:**
- `buildtovalue_kernel_processing_duration_seconds` (p99) > 30ms

**Query Prometheus:**
```promql
histogram_quantile(0.99, 
  rate(buildtovalue_kernel_processing_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])
)
```

**Common Causes:**

**A) Validator Timeout**
```bash
# Check logs for slow validators
kubectl logs -n buildtovalue <pod-name> | grep "VALIDATOR_SLOW"

# Expected output:
# [WARN] VALIDATOR_SLOW: cpf_validator took 45ms (threshold: 30ms)
```

**Solution:**
- Check if CPF blacklist is too large (> 100k entries)
- Verify Bloom filter is loaded correctly
- Consider caching frequently checked patterns

**B) Ring Buffer Contention**
```bash
# Check for lock contention
kubectl logs -n buildtovalue <pod-name> | grep "LOCK_CONTENTION"
```

**Solution:**
- Increase batch size (reduce lock frequency)
- Profile with `cargo flamegraph` to find mutex hotspots

**C) Evidence Finalization Slow**
```promql
# Check finalization time
histogram_quantile(0.99, 
  rate(buildtovalue_evidence_finalization_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])
)
```

**Solution:**
- If > 5ms, check BLAKE3 hashing performance
- Verify fixed-size allocations (no heap growth)

---

### Step 3: Python Governance Slow

**Symptoms:**
- `buildtovalue_governance_processing_duration_seconds` (p99) > 10ms

**Query Prometheus:**
```promql
histogram_quantile(0.99, 
  rate(buildtovalue_governance_processing_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])
)
```

**Common Causes:**

**A) Trust Score Calculation Heavy**
```python
# Check trust score query time
SELECT pg_stat_statements.query, mean_exec_time
FROM pg_stat_statements
WHERE query LIKE '%trust_score%'
ORDER BY mean_exec_time DESC;
```

**Solution:**
- Add index on `user_sessions.session_id`
- Cache trust scores (Redis, TTL 5 min)
- Precompute scores in background job

**B) Profile Loading Slow**
```bash
# Check profile load time
kubectl logs -n buildtovalue <pod-name> | grep "PROFILE_LOAD"

# Expected: < 1ms
# If > 10ms, profiles are too large or not cached
```

**Solution:**
- Enable profile caching (LRU cache, max 100 profiles)
- Reduce profile complexity (fewer rules)
- Preload common profiles at startup

**C) Mercy Algorithm Complex**
```python
# Profile mercy calculation
import cProfile
cProfile.run('mercy_calculator.calculate(evidence, context, trust)')
```

**Solution:**
- Simplify mercy factors (reduce from 5 to 3)
- Cache context justifiability scores
- Precompute harm potential matrix

---

### Step 4: Database Slow

**Symptoms:**
- Query logs show queries > 5ms

**Find Slow Queries:**
```sql
SELECT query, mean_exec_time, calls
FROM pg_stat_statements
WHERE mean_exec_time > 5
ORDER BY mean_exec_time DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

**Common Causes:**

**A) Missing Indexes**
```sql
-- Check index usage
SELECT schemaname, tablename, indexname, idx_scan
FROM pg_stat_user_indexes
WHERE idx_scan = 0 AND schemaname = 'public';

-- Add missing indexes
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_appeals_session_id 
  ON appeals(session_id);
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY idx_user_sessions_timestamp 
  ON user_sessions(timestamp);
```

**B) Table Bloat**
```sql
-- Check table size
SELECT tablename, 
       pg_size_pretty(pg_total_relation_size(tablename::regclass))
FROM pg_tables
WHERE schemaname = 'public'
ORDER BY pg_total_relation_size(tablename::regclass) DESC;

-- Vacuum tables
VACUUM ANALYZE appeals;
VACUUM ANALYZE user_sessions;
```

**C) Connection Pool Exhausted**
```bash
# Check connection count
kubectl exec -it postgres-0 -n buildtovalue -- \
  psql -U btv -d buildtovalue -c \
  "SELECT count(*) FROM pg_stat_activity;"

# If close to max_connections (100), increase pool
```

---

### Step 5: FFI Overhead High

**Symptoms:**
- FFI calls take > 2ms
- Batching not working

**Check Batch Configuration:**
```yaml
# config/production.yaml
batch:
  size: 100          # Should be 100
  timeout_ms: 10     # Should be 10
```

**Solution:**
- Verify batch_scan is being used (not individual scans)
- Check Protobuf serialization overhead
- Profile FFI bridge with `perf`

---

## Quick Fixes (Try First)

### 1. Scale Horizontally
```bash
kubectl scale deployment buildtovalue -n buildtovalue --replicas=6
```

### 2. Restart Pods (Clear Memory)
```bash
kubectl rollout restart deployment/buildtovalue -n buildtovalue
```

### 3. Clear Redis Cache
```bash
kubectl exec -it redis-0 -n buildtovalue -- redis-cli FLUSHDB
```

### 4. Increase Resource Limits
```bash
kubectl set resources deployment/buildtovalue -n buildtovalue \
  --limits=cpu=3,memory=3Gi
```

---

## Long-term Fixes

1. **Profile Hot Paths**
```bash
# Rust profiling
cargo flamegraph --bin buildtovalue_kernel

# Python profiling
py-spy record -o profile.svg -- python -m governance
```

2. **Optimize Queries**
- Add indexes
- Denormalize tables
- Partition large tables

3. **Implement Caching**
- Trust scores (Redis, TTL 5 min)
- Profile configs (LRU cache, 100 entries)
- Validator results (Bloom filter)

4. **Async Operations**
- Move trust score updates to background job
- Async ledger writes (WAL + async flush)
- Non-blocking profile loads
```

#### 19.1.2 Memory Leaks

```markdown
# Issue: Memory Usage Growing Continuously

## Symptoms
- Pods restarting with OOMKilled
- Memory usage grows over time
- HPA scaling up frequently

## Diagnosis

### Step 1: Monitor Memory Growth

**Grafana Dashboard:**
```
Main Dashboard → Resource Usage → Memory panel
```

**Prometheus Query:**
```promql
# Memory usage per pod
container_memory_working_set_bytes{
  namespace="buildtovalue",
  container="buildtovalue"
} / 1024 / 1024  # Convert to MB
```

**Check Growth Rate:**
```promql
# Memory growth rate (MB/hour)
rate(container_memory_working_set_bytes{
  namespace="buildtovalue",
  container="buildtovalue"
}[1h]) * 3600 / 1024 / 1024
```

If growth rate > 10 MB/hour → Likely leak

---

### Step 2: Identify Leak Source

**A) Rust Kernel Leak**

```bash
# Check Rust allocations with Valgrind
kubectl exec -it <pod-name> -n buildtovalue -- \
  valgrind --leak-check=full /app/bin/buildtovalue_kernel

# Or use heaptrack
heaptrack /app/bin/buildtovalue_kernel
heaptrack --analyze heaptrack.buildtovalue_kernel.*.gz
```

**Common Rust Leaks:**
- Ring buffer not clearing old entries
- Evidence not being dropped
- Ledger WAL growing unbounded

**Fix:**
```rust
// Ensure Evidence is dropped after use
impl Drop for TechnicalEvidence {
    fn drop(&mut self) {
        // Explicitly zero sensitive data
        self.findings = [Finding::default(); 10];
        self.critical = [Finding::default(); 3];
    }
}

// Limit WAL size
if self.wal.len() > MAX_WAL_SIZE {
    self.wal.flush_to_disk()?;
}
```

---

**B) Python Governance Leak**

```bash
# Check Python memory with memory_profiler
pip install memory_profiler
python -m memory_profiler governance/main.py

# Or use tracemalloc
import tracemalloc
tracemalloc.start()
# ... run code ...
snapshot = tracemalloc.take_snapshot()
top_stats = snapshot.statistics('lineno')
for stat in top_stats[:10]:
    print(stat)
```

**Common Python Leaks:**
- Circular references (not garbage collected)
- Large objects in global scope
- Unclosed database connections
- Cache without size limit

**Fix:**
```python
# Use weak references for cache
import weakref
cache = weakref.WeakValueDictionary()

# Limit cache size
from functools import lru_cache
@lru_cache(maxsize=1000)
def expensive_function(arg):
    pass

# Close DB connections
try:
    session = db.SessionLocal()
    # ... use session ...
finally:
    session.close()

# Use context managers
with db.SessionLocal() as session:
    # ... use session ...
    pass  # Automatically closed
```

---

**C) Redis Memory Leak**

```bash
# Check Redis memory
kubectl exec -it redis-0 -n buildtovalue -- redis-cli INFO memory

# Check key count
kubectl exec -it redis-0 -n buildtovalue -- redis-cli DBSIZE
```

**Common Issues:**
- Keys without TTL (never expire)
- Large keys (> 1MB)
- Memory not being freed

**Fix:**
```bash
# Set default maxmemory policy
kubectl exec -it redis-0 -n buildtovalue -- \
  redis-cli CONFIG SET maxmemory-policy allkeys-lru

# Find large keys
kubectl exec -it redis-0 -n buildtovalue -- \
  redis-cli --bigkeys

# Set TTL on keys
kubectl exec -it redis-0 -n buildtovalue -- \
  redis-cli EXPIRE key_name 3600  # 1 hour
```

---

### Step 3: Immediate Mitigation

```bash
# Restart leaking pods
kubectl rollout restart deployment/buildtovalue -n buildtovalue

# Increase memory limit (temporary)
kubectl set resources deployment/buildtovalue -n buildtovalue \
  --limits=memory=4Gi

# Enable swap (emergency only, degrades performance)
# Not recommended for production
```

---

### Step 4: Root Cause Fix

**Rust:**
1. Run memory sanitizer:
```bash
cargo build --target x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu -Z build-std \
  --features=address-sanitizer
```

2. Add drop implementations for all large structs

3. Use `Arc` and `Weak` for shared ownership

**Python:**
1. Add garbage collection tuning:
```python
import gc
gc.set_threshold(700, 10, 10)  # More aggressive GC
```

2. Profile with `objgraph`:
```python
import objgraph
objgraph.show_most_common_types(limit=20)
objgraph.show_growth()
```

3. Use `__slots__` to reduce memory:
```python
class TrustScore:
    __slots__ = ['session_id', 'score', 'timestamp']
```

---

## Prevention

1. **Memory Limits**
```yaml
resources:
  limits:
    memory: 2Gi
  requests:
    memory: 512Mi
```

2. **Monitoring**
```promql
# Alert on memory growth
rate(container_memory_working_set_bytes[1h]) > 10485760  # 10MB/hour
```

3. **Load Testing**
```bash
# Run sustained load test (24h)
make load-test-sustained
```

4. **Profiling in CI**
```yaml
# .github/workflows/ci.yml
- name: Memory profiling
  run: cargo test --features memory-profiling
```
```

#### 19.1.3 FFI Issues (Rust ↔ Python)

```markdown
# Issue: FFI Errors / Crashes

## Symptoms
- `FFI_TIMEOUT` errors in logs
- Segmentation faults
- Python crashes
- "Unable to load shared library" errors

## Diagnosis

### Step 1: Verify FFI Bridge is Loaded

```python
# Test FFI loading
import ctypes
lib = ctypes.CDLL('/app/lib/libbuildtovalue_kernel.so')
print("FFI library loaded successfully")
```

**Common Errors:**

**A) Library Not Found**
```
OSError: libbuildtovalue_kernel.so: cannot open shared object file
```

**Fix:**
```bash
# Check library path
ls -la /app/lib/libbuildtovalue_kernel.so

# Set LD_LIBRARY_PATH
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/app/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH

# Verify with ldd
ldd /app/lib/libbuildtovalue_kernel.so
```

**B) ABI Incompatibility**
```
OSError: /app/lib/libbuildtovalue_kernel.so: version `GLIBC_2.34' not found
```

**Fix:**
```dockerfile
# Use compatible base image
FROM rust:1.75-slim-bookworm  # bookworm = glibc 2.36
```

---

### Step 2: Check Function Signatures

**Rust side:**
```rust
// src/kernel/ffi.rs
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn scan_for_evidence(
    input_ptr: *const u8,
    input_len: usize,
    output_ptr: *mut TechnicalEvidence,
) -> i32 {
    // ...
}
```

**Python side:**
```python
# src/governance/ffi_client.py
lib = ctypes.CDLL('/app/lib/libbuildtovalue_kernel.so')

lib.scan_for_evidence.argtypes = [
    ctypes.POINTER(ctypes.c_uint8),  # input_ptr
    ctypes.c_size_t,                  # input_len
    ctypes.POINTER(TechnicalEvidence), # output_ptr
]
lib.scan_for_evidence.restype = ctypes.c_int32
```

**Verify Signatures Match:**
```bash
# Check exported symbols
nm -D /app/lib/libbuildtovalue_kernel.so | grep scan_for_evidence
# Should show: T scan_for_evidence
```

---

### Step 3: Check for Memory Corruption

**Symptoms:**
- Segmentation faults
- Random crashes
- Data corruption

**Common Causes:**

**A) Buffer Overflow**
```rust
// WRONG: No bounds check
pub extern "C" fn process(input_ptr: *const u8, input_len: usize) {
    let slice = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(input_ptr, input_len) };
    // If input_len is wrong, SEGFAULT!
}

// CORRECT: Validate length
pub extern "C" fn process(input_ptr: *const u8, input_len: usize) -> i32 {
    if input_len > MAX_INPUT_SIZE {
        return -1; // Error
    }
    
    if input_ptr.is_null() {
        return -1; // Error
    }
    
    let slice = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(input_ptr, input_len) };
    // Safe now
}
```

**B) Use-After-Free**
```python
# WRONG: Evidence freed before use
evidence_ptr = lib.scan_for_evidence(...)
del evidence_ptr  # Freed!
print(evidence_ptr.finding_count)  # SEGFAULT!

# CORRECT: Keep reference
evidence = TechnicalEvidence()
lib.scan_for_evidence(..., ctypes.byref(evidence))
print(evidence.finding_count)  # Safe
```

**C) Alignment Issues**
```rust
// WRONG: Misaligned struct
#[repr(C)]
pub struct Finding {
    pub title: [u8; 32],     // 32 bytes
    pub confidence: u8,       // 1 byte
    pub severity: u32,        // 4 bytes ← MISALIGNED!
}

// CORRECT: Proper alignment
#[repr(C)]
pub struct Finding {
    pub title: [u8; 32],     // 32 bytes
    pub confidence: u8,       // 1 byte
    pub _padding: [u8; 3],   // 3 bytes padding
    pub severity: u32,        // 4 bytes (now aligned)
}
```

---

### Step 4: Enable Debug Logging

**Rust:**
```rust
// Add debug prints in FFI functions
#[no_mangle]
pub extern "C" fn scan_for_evidence(...) -> i32 {
    eprintln!("[FFI] scan_for_evidence called");
    eprintln!("[FFI] input_len: {}", input_len);
    
    // Process...
    
    eprintln!("[FFI] scan_for_evidence returning: {}", result);
    result
}
```

**Python:**
```python
import logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG)

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
logger.debug(f"Calling FFI with input length: {len(input_text)}")

result = lib.scan_for_evidence(...)

logger.debug(f"FFI returned: {result}")
```

---

### Step 5: Test FFI in Isolation

```python
# test_ffi_minimal.py

import ctypes

# Load library
lib = ctypes.CDLL('/app/lib/libbuildtovalue_kernel.so')

# Test simple function (no complex structs)
lib.add.argtypes = [ctypes.c_int, ctypes.c_int]
lib.add.restype = ctypes.c_int

result = lib.add(5, 3)
print(f"5 + 3 = {result}")  # Should print 8

# If this works, library is loaded correctly
# If this fails, check LD_LIBRARY_PATH
```

---

## Quick Fixes

### 1. Rebuild FFI Library
```bash
cd src/kernel
cargo clean
cargo build --release
```

### 2. Verify Library Path
